newsitem.title: USA: Clinton - US could join global anti-tobacco effort.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - US could join global anti-tobacco effort.

text.p: President Bill Clinton suggested on Wednesday that the United States might participate in international efforts aimed at curbing sales of tobacco, especially to children.
"I think that there may be some multilateral actions that we would want to be part of," Clinton said in response to a question about possible efforts to slow tobacco sales overseas.

"I know that sales have been declining in the United States and Latin America and going up in Asia and in Eastern Europe, and that it's natural to expect that the companies will try to accelerate the growing markets," he said at a White House news conference.
"If they're dangerous to children here, they're dangerous to children there," he said.

Clinton said he was now evaluating a proposed settlement between the tobacco industry and the state attorneys general in which cigarette manufacturers promised to pay out $368 billion, partly to reimburse states for smoking-related health costs and partly to fund anti-smoking efforts.
However, Clinton noted that "it is inevitable as the sun coming up today that international institutions will be called upon and nations will be called upon to responsively deal with this."
